findings.title: Two gate clauses say 'readable record' after walk 2 widened unreadable for this record
findings.recommendation: Walk 2 (external W3) made a walk the trail reader reads ALSO unreadable for the verification record when an entry normalizes to an empty title or file. The write-gate clause 'a walk_entry naming a key carried by no readable record of verified_walks' and the shared-key waiver's 'every entry carrying that key in verified_walks' do not say which sense they use. Qualify both as 'readable for this record (per the owed-set paragraph)', so a stale entry in a walk with an unnameable sibling is unambiguously not linkable and not counted in the waiver.

findings.title: Task 1.3 does not render the walk that is unreadable only for the record
findings.recommendation: Walk 2 added the empty-key case to the render spec's unreadable-row sentence and to task 1.2's write-gate fixtures, but task 1.3's render list still names only a generic 'unreadable-walk row'. Add the case: a walk the trail reader reads, holding a resolved entry with no title, renders '- walk <token> — unreadable; nothing owed'.

commentary: VERIFICATION by the pass-genre table: one qualifying walk (the external pass's walk) follows the latest accepted independent pass. Each of its four resolutions was checked against the artifacts and landed: the absent-field refusal now names every owed key, the residual kind names the co-commit limit with a scenario, the empty-key walk is unreadable for the record in the owed-set paragraph and the render sentence, and the landed-link refusal is narrowed to all-resolved keys with the gap declared in the requirement and design Risks. Walk 1's nine resolutions were also re-read where walk 2 touched the same sentences and still hold. The passes then ran over the walks' additions; the two residues are both the same shape the cycle keeps finding — a widening in one sentence that two neighbouring sentences and one task did not follow. No engine record of this pass's genre exists yet: that is what this change ships.
